title: Example 286: the three answers beside the route again, with the driver's record of what it ran (evidence.json)
description: The evidence stream's acceptance check (examples/tools/accept.py) accepts an answer given beside the route only with no limit when the driver recorded what it ran: the JARs of the class path with their hashes, the adapter's sources and compiled classes, the claim file, the bound and the verifier's binary (evidence.json, written by accept.record). Every example's proofs/prove.py now does this through examples/tools/beside_route.py, and ends the run when the mutant's JAR is not the one the mutant replay's receipt records. Example 286's mutant-security is refused today: the old driver built its mutant with another recipe, so the mutant's JAR hash is in no record (and was not the replay's bytes). This job reruns vulnerable-security, fixed-security (with its simpleMatch lemma, proved first under the checker's tightened lemma checks) and mutant-security unchanged at the frozen bound into a work folder of their own (verification/.work-286/recorded), so the earlier jobs' outputs stay as their results record them. When it has passed, each task's besideRoute.job is switched to it and python3 examples/tools/accept.py 286 must accept all three with no limit.
expected: exits 0: prove.py prints violation, verified and violation, each the expected one, at the frozen bound; each task's outcome.json and evidence.json come back

resources.notes: the earlier jobs took 501 s (vulnerable), 1015 s (fixed, with the lemma) and 492 s (mutant) at 1.4 to 1.6 GiB; plus the release build of lib/ (about 3 min, 2.3 GiB) and the fetch of the pinned JARs
